title: Leche flan
intro: A dense, silky custard of egg yolks and milk, steamed in llaneras over a layer of caramel that turns into a dark, glossy sauce. It is rich, sweet and smooth, and it shows up at almost every handaan.

steps.text: Put 0.5 cup sugar in each llanera. Hold one at a time over low heat with tongs and let the sugar melt without stirring, swirling now and then, until it turns deep amber.
Take the llanera off the heat and tilt it so the caramel coats the whole bottom. Set aside; the caramel hardens and may crackle as it cools, which is fine.
Put the yolks in a bowl and add the condensed milk, evaporated milk, vanilla and zest. Stir gently with a spoon until smooth. Do not whisk hard: bubbles leave holes in the flan.
Strain the mixture twice through a fine sieve, then pour it over the caramel. Cover each llanera tightly with foil.
Bring water to a boil in a steamer, then lower the heat so it only simmers. Wrap the lid in a kitchen towel so drips do not fall on the flan.
Steam the llaneras over low heat until the flan is set and a toothpick near the center comes out clean.
Lift out the llaneras, remove the foil and let the flan cool to room temperature.
Chill for at least 4 hours. To serve, run a thin knife around the edge, put a plate on top and flip it over so the caramel runs down the sides.

tips: A rolling boil makes the flan spongy and full of holes, so keep the steamer at a gentle simmer. Overnight chilling gives the cleanest slices. Save the egg whites for meringue or silvanas, or freeze them.

title: Ube halaya
intro: Purple yam cooked slowly with butter and milk until thick, smooth and glossy, then packed into llaneras. It is sweet, buttery and earthy, eaten on its own, spread on bread or spooned into halo-halo.

items.name: ube (purple yam)
items.note: or 1 kg frozen grated ube, thawed

items.name: butter
items.note: 113 g, plus more for the llaneras

steps.text: Scrub the ube and boil it whole in water to cover until a fork slides in easily. Skip this and the next step if you are using frozen grated ube.
Drain, let the ube cool enough to handle, then peel and grate it finely or mash it until smooth.
Melt the butter in a wide, heavy nonstick pan over low heat. Add the ube, condensed milk, evaporated milk and sugar and stir until smooth.
Cook over low heat, stirring and scraping the bottom constantly, until the mixture is very thick and pulls away from the pan as one mass.
Stir in the ube flavoring and taste; add a little more sugar if you like it sweeter and cook a minute more.
Butter two llaneras, pack the halaya in and smooth the tops. Let it cool.
Sprinkle with grated cheese if you like, and serve at room temperature or chilled.

tips: A wide pan and a sturdy wooden spatula make the long stirring easier, and the stirring is what makes halaya smooth. It keeps 1 week in the fridge or 2 months in the freezer.

title: Halo-halo
intro: Shaved ice layered over sweetened fruits, beans and jellies, drenched in evaporated milk and crowned with ube halaya, leche flan, ice cream and crisp pinipig. You mix it all together and eat it with a long spoon on a hot afternoon.

steps.text: Chill all the sweetened fruits, beans and jellies in their syrups ahead of time, so the halo-halo stays cold longer.
Spoon about 1 tablespoon of each layer ingredient into the bottom of 4 tall glasses, with a little of their syrup.
Pack the shaved ice on top, pressing lightly and mounding it above the rim.
Pour 0.25 cup evaporated milk over the ice in each glass.
Top each with a spoonful of ube halaya, a slice of leche flan, a scoop of ice cream and a sprinkle of pinipig. Serve right away with long spoons and mix before eating.

tips: Use whatever five or six sweets you have, as long as there is fruit, something chewy, beans and milk. No ice shaver? Pulse ice cubes in a blender in short bursts until fluffy.

title: Buko pandan
intro: Tender young coconut strips and cubes of pandan gulaman folded into sweet cream and condensed milk, served very cold. It is creamy, fragrant and a party favorite next to the fruit salad.

steps.text: Boil the water with the pandan leaves to draw out their flavor, then remove the leaves.
Mix the gulaman powder with the sugar, whisk it into the hot pandan water and boil, stirring, until fully dissolved. Stir in the flavoring.
Pour into a square pan and let it set at room temperature until firm.
Cut the gulaman into small cubes.
Stir the cream and condensed milk together in a large bowl.
Fold in the gulaman cubes, coconut strips and sago.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours until very cold. Serve in cups.

tips: If the young coconut is a bit mature and thick, slice it into thin strips so it stays tender. It keeps 2 days in the fridge; after that the gulaman starts to weep.
